object.label: H1c — the price leg read by the vote, from the LI corner, three days on: the holder's house conceding the mechanism while the holder's office polices the blame. The tape's object is the WSJ memo — 'we are monitoring statements, press releases, and media engagements from your organizations', to over 3,000 conservative groups — and its vehicle is the mob boss (Tony Soprano, Kim Jong-un, the golden ballroom). Under the vehicle, the predicate in its plainest form yet from inside the holder's family: Don Jr. — 'whether you think it was the right decision or not, the Iran war is largely what shifted voter sentiment… it jacked up the price of gas'. The unnamed Republican's instruction read off the vote — lower gas prices, lower food prices, lower interest rates — with the war absent. The panel: 'it was the gas prices', 'the Iran war was a problem', 'we saw that in the voter poll'; it was not a surprise why, only how big

zAxis.pos: the war did not cost the vote — the loss has another cause or another owner

object.gear: fast — the pump and the vote; the memo and the mob boss are shadow (who may be blamed); the slow gear not on any line

transformNote: the holder's promise — diesel 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST' (10-11) — is not on the tape. What is on it is the apparatus for managing who says what about the cost: a memo to 3,000 groups listing accomplishments and ending with 'we are monitoring'. The shadow on this tape is institutional — the reading policed rather than asserted. Against it, the holder's son states the mechanism (the war → gas → the vote) without a quantifier and the panel treats it as what 'any human being who was buying gas' already knew. The tape's own vehicle (the mob boss, North Korea) carries the two highest lines
